audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may not be fully captured
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,033 million ARO at December 31, 2025; $122 million of 2025 settlements, equal to 31.2% of the $390.7 million anchor OE; liability increased to $1,049 million at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring abandonment settlements reduce OE; any unfunded residual obligation not represented in normalized OE requires an equity-bridge deduction without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had asset retirement obligations of $1,033 million and $1,129 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and substantial cash settlements are demonstrated, but omission from OE is not established because the OE workpaper is absent. The scale is material: the year-end liability equals 19.3% of the $5,348 million base equity value, and 2025 settlements equal nearly one-third of anchor OE. Capitalizing OE that excludes sustainable settlements could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 and 2026 ARO settlements to the OE calculation, estimate sustainable enlarged-company abandonment cash spending from filed schedules, and rerun after including either recurring settlements in OE or the unfunded residual in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Brookfield’s contingent repayment claim may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $123 million recognized liability at June 30, 2026, or $1.34 per diluted share; 2.3% of base equity value; additional development contributions are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The claim is a liability associated with the Carbon TerraVault investment credited through stakes_net and therefore may require a separate bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Because the parties have certain put and call rights (repurchase features) with respect to the 26R reservoir if certain milestones are not met, the initial investment (including accrued interest) by Brookfield is reflected as a contingent liability included in other long-term liabilities on our consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed contingent liability exceeds the $98 million stakes addition by $25 million. Deducting the recognized $123 million would reduce base value from $58.40 to approximately $57.06 per share, which alone would not reverse the comparison with the $54.22 market price. However, the filed liability excludes qualifying development contributions included in the exercise payment, and the record does not quantify them or establish whether the bridge already offsets the claim.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $98 million stakes_net balance to each equity-method investment, confirm whether the $123 million liability is separately included, obtain the total put/call exercise amount including accrued interest and development contributions, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Offshore decommissioning indemnity may exceed the recognized reserve
audit_findings.magnitude: $23 million accrued at June 30, 2026, or $0.25 per diluted share; $20 million of expense in the first half of 2026; excess exposure is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Ongoing maintenance and abandonment spending reduces OE, while any probable unfunded ultimate indemnity requires an equity-bridge deduction unless already captured through normalized OE or ARO.
audit_findings.evidence: Oxy notified us of the claim under the indemnification provisions of the Separation and Distribution Agreement between us and Oxy.
audit_findings.explanation: The accepted indemnity, current spending and $23 million accrual are demonstrated. The recognized amount is only 0.4% of the $5,348 million base equity value, but CRC states that reasonably possible losses beyond reserves cannot be determined. The record therefore cannot establish the ultimate materiality or overlap with recorded ARO.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the platform-and-well decommissioning estimate, CRC’s contractual share, timing, recoveries and overlap with ARO; then include recurring spending in OE and deduct only the remaining unfunded obligation.

audit_findings.title: The anchor numerator and share denominator cover different Berry periods
audit_findings.magnitude: 5.572 million merger shares, approximately 6% of post-close ownership, are in the denominator while 2025 includes only 14 days of Berry; those 14 days contributed $18 million of revenue and a $25 million pretax loss; pro forma 2025 revenue was $4,298 million versus $3,669 million reported and pro forma net income was $329 million versus $363 million reported; OE effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The full post-merger diluted share count divides an OE anchor containing only a partial period of Berry operations, financing, sustaining capital, ARO settlements and integration costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Our consolidated results of operations include the results of Berry beginning December 18, 2025, the closing date of the Berry Merger.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated and affects the core numerator-denominator consistency of every scenario. Direction is not reliably conservative: a full year adds Berry operations but also full financing costs, sustaining capital and abandonment spending, while filed pro forma net income was $34 million below reported net income. Given Berry’s ownership and revenue scale, a perimeter-consistent OE result could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Construct a full-year combined-company OE reconciliation using filed Berry and CRC results, full-year interest, sustaining capital, ARO settlements and recurring integration costs; exclude unsupported synergies and rerun all scenarios with the same diluted share basis.

audit_findings.title: A known resource-adequacy revenue step-down is embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed expected 2026 revenue decline of $125 million to $135 million, equal to 53.6% to 57.9% of 2025 electricity revenue and 32.0% to 34.6% of anchor OE on a gross-revenue scale; first-half 2026 electricity revenue declined $63 million year over year, from $80 million to $17 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The known revenue reset lowers normalized anchor OE before scenario growth is applied and terminalized.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, we expect that our 2026 revenues from resource adequacy contracts will decrease between $125 million to $135 million in 2026 as compared to 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The step-down is demonstrated rather than hypothetical, and first-half 2026 results confirm that it began occurring. The OE impact is smaller than the gross revenue loss because associated variable costs and taxes must be considered, but their amount is not supplied. The gross scale is sufficiently large relative to $390.7 million anchor OE to be reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 resource-adequacy revenue and associated generation costs and taxes to 2026 actuals, normalize anchor OE for the net after-tax decline, and rerun every scenario from that adjusted anchor.

audit_findings.title: Unrealized derivative marks could contaminate owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 contained a $225 million noncash commodity-derivative gain and a $24 million noncash natural-gas-purchase derivative loss, producing a $201 million net pretax unrealized gain, equal to 51.4% of anchor OE; actual net settlements were $15 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrealized fair-value marks must be removed from the OE numerator, while cash settlements and recurring economic hedge effects must be retained exactly once.
audit_findings.evidence: Since we did not apply hedge accounting to our commodity derivatives for any of the periods presented, we recognized fair value adjustments, on a net basis, in our consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Contamination is not demonstrated because the detailed OE reconciliation is not supplied. If the marks were left in, however, the $201 million net noncash gain would materially overstate the anchor and be repeatedly capitalized. Its scale relative to anchor OE makes this an open material validation issue rather than a minor disclosure gap.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2025 OE workpaper and reconcile GAAP income to OE line by line, subtracting the $225 million noncash gain, adding back the $24 million noncash loss, retaining the $41 million production-derivative proceeds and $26 million fuel-derivative settlements exactly once, then rerun if the reconciliation differs.
